speaker: Doctor
text: I notice your skin and eyes appear yellowish, which suggests jaundice. Can you tell me if you have experienced any abdominal pain, nausea, or changes in the color of your urine or stool recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior, I need to rule out viral hepatitis. Have you noticed any dark-colored urine or pale, clay-colored stools in addition to the jaundice?

speaker: Doctor
text: To help narrow down the cause of your hepatitis and agitation, have you experienced any fever, dark urine, or pale stools recently? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests, Hepatitis_Panel, CBC

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Bilirubin: 25 mg/dL (elevated), AST: 600 IU/L (elevated), ALT: 650 IU/L (elevated), TP_Activity: < 40% (reduced), INR: 1.5 (elevated)

speaker: Doctor
text: These lab results indicate severe acute liver failure, which is likely causing your agitation through hepatic encephalopathy. To pinpoint the specific cause, I need to know if you have had any recent fevers, chills, or unexplained weight loss? REQUEST TEST: Ammonia_level, Acetaminophen_level

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal ammonia and acetaminophen levels, we must look closely at the hepatitis panel results to determine if this is caused by Hepatitis A, B, or C. Do you recall any recent travel, consumption of raw shellfish, or close contact with someone who was sick before your symptoms began?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe acute liver failure and your history of high-risk sexual behavior, viral hepatitis B is the most likely culprit. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Hepatitis B
